newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close firmer, small caps shine.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close firmer, small caps shine.

text.p: Singapore shares closed broadly firmer on Monday with bulk of the activity dominated by small capitalised issues.
"It is still small caps and all the recently listed issues. Many of them hit new highs today," said a dealer with a Singapore brokerage.
Among the most active was auto parts distributor Tye Soon Ltd which touched a new high of Singapore $0.615 before closing at S$0.61 with over 13 million units traded.
Other small caps which touched new highs included telephone cord maker Huan Hsin at US$0.585, disk drive component MMI Holdings at S$0.82 and packaging company New Toyo at S$1.04.
Dealers said most counters closed off their highs as there were some profit taking before the close of trading.
The Straits Times Industrial index closed off its intraday high of 2,007.63, at 1,997.99, up 12.05 points.
Total market volume was a brisk 200.15 million shares with 243 gainers beating 137 losers.
Dealers expected the market to remain firm ahead of the budget this Friday.
"It is expected to be pro-business so there is some buying of blue chips," said one broker.
Among the gainers are the foreign tranches of banks like DBS Bank and United Overseas Bank, both gaining 60 cents each.
Singapore Press foreign touched a new high of S$30.40 before closing at S$30.20 in active trading with over 714,000 shares traded.
Topping the losers list was Thai cellular phone company Total Access Communications which shed 57 cents to US$4.98. A dealer said the fall mirrored the weaker Thai stock market.
